title: Reject finance application exchange rates that cannot survive actual persistence
description: Close deposit/payment application rate persistence gap independently of amount tasks508/509. Both NormalizeExchangeRate check raw>0 then round6 without checking rounded>0; tiny positive input rounds to zero. Finance1.ExchangeRate has no explicit EF precision, actual SQL default18,2, so positive6-decimal rate may silently change or become zero at persistence, and huge rates overflow SQL. Preserve existing six-decimal normalization intent, but separately reject a normalized rate that cannot round-trip through the actual target column unchanged; no silent coarser rounding, schema change or inferred rate. Confirm actual EF and SQL metadata in isolated tests first. All accepted normalized rates must remain positive and exactly stored. Apply at existing create/update before numbering and operational persisted consistency under locks; keep historical rate comparison/read/void helpers unchanged and no new undo gate. Reuse existing layers, authority, source ownership, transactions/locks and audited service writes. No schema/migration, new grants or production access. Do not cap global CurrencyAmountRules or legitimate read-side aggregates. Do not silently repair historical snapshots; preserve historical read/void/cancel and existing undo semantics. Adapt related original fixtures with genuine live identities/masters and original assertions intact. Exact explicit logs/TRX/results under .ai/logs/<task> only; retain complete original failed logs and accurate real environment blockers. Retain existing live identity/menu/customer-scope authority, transactions, source locks, controlled errors and audit. Reject before numbering or persistence, with zero header/detail/source/status mutations. No new permissions, schema, production access, external service or arbitrary SQL. Genuine SQL only on (localdb)\NEWERP_AutoAcceptance with Integrated Security and a fresh GUID-owned NEWERP_AUTOTEST database; reject wrong/existing targets and never drop/reset. Require safe Release with analyzers/warnings-as-errors, full units and relevant genuine SQL/browser tests; accurately record blockers and do not claim whole-stage acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Both application types refuse nonpositive normalized rates, CLR-scale/range overflow and rates not exactly representable in actual target SQL storage, before number reservation or header/source writes. Preserve current six-decimal normalization behavior for representable values and supported amount/currency rules; no implicit exchange conversion/schema change.

Submit/approve revalidates positive exact stored rates within existing document/source locks, refusing malformed legacy snapshots without rewriting them. Preserve supplier/customer/source ownership, budgets, approval/cancel and immutable historical evidence; authority remains fail closed.

Meaningful unit/controller and genuine isolated SQL verify EF and physical rate precision, tiny raw positives normalizing to0, positive rates SQL would coarsen to0/change, exact legal boundary/huge values, accepted round-trip and linked/manual lifecycle plus denied zero writes/numbering. Run existing deposit/payment application canonical entry, source, concurrency and cancellation SQL regressions and safe Release/full units.
implementation_evidence: FinanceDepositApplyLifecycleRules.NormalizeExchangeRate:145 and FinancePaymentApplyLifecycleRules counterpart check exchangeRate<=0 BEFORE Round6 and return rounded unchecked. Finance1.ExchangeRate has no HasPrecision; Config only unique apply numbers. Existing amount tasks508/509 explicitly exclude rate/schema changes. Tiny .0000001 becomes0; rate.001 normalized6 reaches SQLdefault2 and loses positive value. No rate round-trip task found in history/docs; ERP-426 handles purchase-order rates only.
